 Learn more ServiceNow (NOW) is back in the spotlight after a run of AI centric announcements, from its Arc personal agent launch with NVIDIA to fresh customer deployments at Thrive and Boardwalktech. 
 For context, ServiceNow's share price has climbed over recent weeks, with a 7-day share price return of 8.82%, a 30-day gain of 16.63%, and a 90-day move of 42.99% to around US$158. However, the 1-year total shareholder return is still down 16.42% and the 5-year total shareholder return is 15.97%, which points to momentum rebuilding in the short term, while longer term holders have seen more modest progress overall. 
 Scan how other AI focused platforms are moving by comparing ServiceNow's setup with the hand picked 55 AI infrastructure stocks , which may also be riding this workflow and automation wave. 
 Bulls point to ServiceNow's AI traction and fresh partnerships, while bears focus on the recent share price surge and past 1-year drawdown. Which side does current valuation actually support next? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 39% Undervalued 
 ServiceNow's most followed storyline pegs fair value at about $260.58 per share, well above the last close around $158. This frames today's AI excitement against a much larger long term cash flow picture. 
 The market may still see a software company. I increasingly see a utility for the digital economy. And if that assessment is correct, ServiceNow's most profitable decade may not be behind it. Every great investment begins with a disagreement. The bulls believe ServiceNow is building the infrastructure layer for the AI-powered enterprise. The bears believe it is simply another software company approaching maturity. Which side of that debate do you think history will prove correct? 
 See why 96 investors see ServiceNow as 39% undervalued . 
 Result: Fair Value of $260.58 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, the bullish ServiceNow story can crack if AI workflows stall with large customers or if its acquisition driven debt load starts to weigh on its flexibility. 
 Find out about the key risks to this ServiceNow narrative . 
 Another View: What Multiples Say About ServiceNow 
 Zoom out from cash flows and look at simple pricing ratios and the picture changes. ServiceNow trades on a P/E of 97.9x, while the US Software industry averages 32.7x and peers sit near 33.4x. The fair ratio sits at 51.5x. That gap signals real valuation risk if sentiment cools. Which signal would you trust under pressure? 
 Investors who prefer to anchor on earnings-based pricing can use this gap as a sanity check on their own thesis. See what the numbers say about this price — find out in our valuation breakdown.
